title: Zhai
capsule: Zhai, also called the Kingdom of Di, was one of the Three Qins, the successor states Xiang Yu carved from the former Qin dynasty's Guanzhong heartland in 206 BC after the Qin collapse. Its king was the surrendered Qin general Dong Yi, enfeoffed as King of Di with a capital at Gaonu in the region's north, ruling alongside the neighboring kingdoms of Yong and Sai. Zhai's independence was short-lived: Liu Bang's forces stormed back into Guanzhong later in 206 BC and Dong Yi surrendered without a fight, after which Zhai's territory was absorbed into the emerging Han dynasty — a wholly different polity from the earlier Qin dynasty it splintered from.
